title: Wavelength Dispersive Spectrometry (WDS) - Is There Something Better Than Gas Flow X-Ray Detectors?
content: Gas flow proportional counters (GFPC’s) have been used in wavelength dispersive spectrometers (WDS) since Castaing produced his prototype instrument in 1951 [1]. Their design has remained largely unchanged in the last 65 years. At the time, GFPC’s offered several benefits: 1) detection of x-rays over a wide energy range, 2) the output voltage is proportional to the detected x-ray energy, 3) automatic amplification via gas gain, and 4) rudimentary energy filtering providing some level of high-order overlap correction. However, they also come with several significant weaknesses: sensitivity to temperature, pressure and even relative humidity [2], which all affect the counter efficiency; the energy filtering is insufficient as the counter energy response varies with input count rate [3]. These weaknesses drive the need for frequent recalibration.
